newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares drift lower in dull trading.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares drift lower in dull trading.

text.p: Limited profit-taking by domestic institutionals pressured prices of shares at the Athens stock exchange on Thursday on the back of Wednesday's strong blue chip performance, according to market watchers.

"During the past few sessions, domestic institutional portfolios play a more important role in the market, volumewise, but they refrain from pushing stock prices higher or lower." said Thanos Trikatzis, a broker with Hermes Securities.

"Investors appear to have lost their appetite for construction stocks in favour of select industrial and banking blue chips. The rally in large banking stocks has started to percolate to smaller banks, too, eliminating price imbalances," he added.

The Athens general share index drifted 6.04 points or 0.44 percent lower from Wednesday's 1,375.10 to close at 1,369.06. Turnover was moderate at 11.7 billion drachmas on volume of 3.4 million shares.
Decliners led advancers 142 to 74 with 20 issues unchanged on 236 traded.

Banks which continue to lead the broader market trend, like they have done since the begining of the current year, fell 0.61 percent with industrials slipping 0.58 percent. But construction dropped a sharper 1.5 percent.
Investors continued to reward Ionian Bank and Commercial Bank for their efforts to cleanse their balance sheets, with buyers outweighing sellers.

OTE closed 40 drachmas higher at 6,050 on growing indications of an acceleration of its investment programme, while Titan Cement edged 0.61pct higher to 20,505 on reports of superior fiscal 1996 performance, brokers said.
